A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching methods, theorems, datasets, and original experiments. The main text, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite renumbering and added material.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation experiments on a hyperplane, triangular meshes, SO(10), and alanine dipeptide, plus hyperparameter sensitivity results in Appendix E.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds evaluated RSSM comparisons, additional sensitivity results, and sampling runtime measurements.

M1.justification: The Niso-DM perturbation and loss, Tango-DM loss switching, rescaling, and sampling Algorithms 1–3 retain the same procedures. Newly documented mesh implementation details do not establish an algorithm change. Appendix F.2 explicitly leaves the autoencoder extension for future work.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same hyperplane mixture, Bunny and Cow meshes, SO(10) mixture, and constrained alanine distribution. The additional sensitivity and runtime experiments use retained tasks. Learned manifolds are discussed but not evaluated.

E2.justification: v1 compares the proposed methods with Iso and Iso+res variants. v2 adds Riemannian sliced score matching (RSSM) to both mesh comparisons and the SO(10) comparison in Tables 1–2. This substantially broadens the comparison scope by introducing an evaluated Riemannian diffusion baseline.

E3.justification: The reported alanine metric changes from 1-Wasserstein in v1 Table 4 to 2-Wasserstein in v2 Table 3, although every numerical entry remains identical; the PDFs do not establish whether this corrects a label or reflects recomputation. Appendix F.1 adds a runtime comparison using five versus ten inner Langevin steps. Existing splits and main hyperparameter settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 3's sensitivity analyses are retained, and v2 Tables 6, 7, and 9 tabulate existing plotted analyses. Table 8 adds a sigma-minimum sweep, although its Tango caption conflicts with its Niso row label. Appendix F.1 also adds a sampling-cost analysis varying the inner Langevin step count.

E5.justification: Both versions report the main comparisons as means and standard deviations over five independent runs, and Figure 3 retains mean curves with standard-deviation shading. Additional result rows introduce no new uncertainty procedure, seed policy, or significance test.

E6.justification: The original benchmark means and standard deviations are retained. New results include RSSM's SO(10) distance of 7.14e-3 ± 9.09e-4, additional Table 8 values with ambiguous method labeling, and runtimes of 1.68 seconds for Reverse SDE versus 5.62 or 9.40 seconds for Annealing SDE. Alanine's unchanged values receive a different metric label, so they do not establish a comparable performance change.

T1.justification: The central theorem statements remain, but v2 corrects the VPSDE drift sign and missing factors of two in Appendix C.1, revises proof normalization factors, and formally states a local-boundedness relaxation in Appendix F.3. These are localized mathematical revisions. The revised prefactor in v2 Eq. (45), however, is inconsistent with Eqs. (40) and (46).

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same core contributions: tangential/normal score asymptotics, Niso-DM and Tango-DM, and improved generation on complex known manifolds. Added comparisons support these existing claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds qualifications about nonsmooth mesh applicability, a speculative geometric-bottleneck explanation for RSSM's mesh performance, Tango's sampling cost, and the dependence of a future autoencoder extension on manifold reconstruction accuracy. The known-manifold requirement and Tango's general incompatibility with Reverse SDE were already stated in v1.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code URL and states that code and data are available. Appendix D newly documents the RSSM loss and mesh projection, edge handling, and normal-selection rules. Figure 1 newly specifies sigma_min = 0.01, and Appendix F.1 supplies runtime and laptop context. The existing architecture, optimization, GPU, and main hyperparameter disclosures are retained.

R1.justification: Section 7 substantially expands positioning through intrinsic-dimension, spectral, and generalization research, plus a dedicated comparison with Horvat and Pfister's inflation-deflation approach. v2 acknowledges antecedents to score-scale separation and normal-direction noise, then distinguishes its diffusion setting, assumptions, and score asymptotics. This goes beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The main narrative and section sequence largely survive. v2 polishes wording and mathematical explanations, revises the experiment introduction, renames Appendix E, and adds separate limitations and discussion sections, acknowledgments, an impact statement, and the conference checklist. The retained scientific exposition is refined rather than extensively reorganized.

P2.justification: All three figures retain the same artwork; Figure 1's caption gains a setting disclosure. The hyperplane table moves from the main text to Appendix D as Table 5. RSSM rows and four compact ablation tables are added, with corresponding caption and page-layout adjustments. The overall visual format remains stable.

improvement.justification: The RSSM comparisons, explicit mesh implementation rules, and computational and applicability discussion provide a modest net improvement in how the work can be assessed and reproduced. These benefits are tempered by the unexplained alanine metric relabeling, Table 8's conflicting method label, and the normalization inconsistency in v2 Appendix A.
